blockMcqs.question: What does an LLD interviewer actually grade you on?
options: How many users the system can scale to
How cheaply the design absorbs a new requirement
Whether the code runs on the first try
How many design patterns you name
blockMcqs.explanation: "It works" is the floor; the score is whether change stays a small patch.

blockMcqs.question: Which step of the recipe earns points by showing you don't gold-plate?
options: Drawing the full class diagram first
Clarifying and narrowing scope up front
Applying as many patterns as possible
blockMcqs.explanation: Pinning down what's in and out of scope signals you avoid over-engineering.

blockMcqs.question: A ParkingLot owns its Levels. Which relationship is that?
blockMcqs.explanation: A container owning its parts is composition, the workhorse relationship.

blockMcqs.question: Adding a payment type by writing a new class, not editing a switch, is which principle?
blockMcqs.explanation: Extending behavior without modifying existing code is the open/closed idea.

blockMcqs.question: Pricing has interchangeable variants. Which pattern fits?
blockMcqs.explanation: Swapping an algorithm behind an injected interface is exactly Strategy.

blockMcqs.question: Why a doubly-linked list rather than a singly-linked one for an LRU cache?
options: It uses less memory per node
It keeps keys in sorted order
Any node can be unlinked and moved in O(1)
It allows binary search over the list
blockMcqs.explanation: prev and next pointers let you detach any node without scanning to find it.

blockMcqs.question: What is the time complexity of LRU get and put?
blockMcqs.explanation: A hash lookup plus a fixed number of pointer rewires never scans the data.

blockMcqs.question: Vehicles vary by both size and fuel type. Why does inheritance struggle?
options: It can only model one axis of variation
It is slower at runtime than composition
It forbids more than two subclasses
blockMcqs.explanation: A single tree forces one hierarchy; composition mixes the axes freely.

blockMcqs.question: A status field drives a behavior switch repeated across many methods. Use which pattern?
blockMcqs.explanation: Each mode becomes a class owning its own transitions, killing the scattered switch.

blockMcqs.question: Passing a Comparator to a sort routine is an example of which pattern?
blockMcqs.explanation: The sort stays closed while you supply a swappable ordering algorithm.

blockMcqs.question: Why are getters and setters on every field not real encapsulation?
options: They are slower than public fields
They still leak the internal shape and allow invalid states
They make the class a Singleton
blockMcqs.explanation: Encapsulation exposes intentions like car.park(spot), not raw internal data.
